event.summary: Influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate were arrested by US federal authorities in Miami on a sealed warrant. The United Kingdom is seeking their extradition to face 38 new charges, including rape, sex trafficking, and assault. This brings the total number of charges against them in the UK to 59.

event_overview.title: About Tate Brothers Arrest
event_overview.subject: Tate Brothers Arrest
event_overview.summary: The event concerns the July 2026 U.S. arrest of Andrew and Tristan Tate after UK prosecutors sought their extradition to face criminal charges in England. It is an extradition and charging matter, not a finding of guilt: the Crown Prosecution Service says the proceedings are active and that guilt can be determined only by a court.

facts.label: Arrest and location
facts.value: The brothers were arrested by the U.S. Marshals Service in the United States on July 18, 2026; reporting and the selected timeline identify Miami, Florida, as the location of the arrest.

facts.label: UK charging scope
facts.value: The CPS said it would pursue extradition on 21 pre-existing charges and further charges involving four additional alleged victims. The added allegations include rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, assault, and offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.

facts.label: Alleged time period and victims
facts.value: According to the CPS, the further alleged offending occurred between July 2010 and August 2017; the charging decisions brought the stated total number of alleged victims in the UK case to seven.

facts.label: Earlier extradition history
facts.value: UK extradition warrants were issued at Westminster Magistrates’ Court in January 2024. In March 2024, the Bucharest Court of Appeal ordered extradition to the UK only after separate Romanian criminal proceedings concluded.

facts.label: Legal status
facts.value: The CPS requested extradition from the United States, and as of July 19, 2026 said the brothers had been arrested and were awaiting extradition proceedings. The CPS emphasizes that a charging decision is not a finding of fact or guilt and that the defendants have a right to a fair trial.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the Miami arrest and the initial U.S. extradition challenge from July 19–21, 2026, rather than the underlying evidence, the separate Romanian proceedings, or any eventual extradition or trial outcome.
